lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- The Interview
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Gabriel Fernandes | Lesson 3 -- The Interview

listenings.text: People ask me what makes a good interview, and they always expect me to say confidence. It is not confidence. The best conversations I have had were with candidates who hesitated, because hesitating usually means somebody is actually thinking. What I am listening for is whether the person can elaborate. I ask a small question, and a rehearsed candidate gives me the paragraph they prepared and then stops. A genuine one gives me two sentences and then keeps going, because the thing is real and there is more of it. I also notice what they ask me. If somebody has no questions at the end, I write that down, and I do not write it down as a good thing.

My interview was thirty minutes and I remember about four of them. What I remember is being asked what I do that nobody makes me do, and hearing myself talk about the food bank on Sunday mornings for far longer than I meant to. I had prepared an answer about a science prize, and I never used it. Afterwards my mother asked me whether I had asked her anything, and I had not, so I sent an email that night. I asked how she had chosen her own subject, and she wrote back a long answer. I do not know if that email changed anything. I know that it cost me ten minutes and that I would do it again.

extra_audio.text: You are shortlisted, and an email invites you to choose a time. You write back to ask whether the meeting will be online or in person. The interviewer opens by asking you to tell her about yourself. Near the end she asks whether you would like to ask her anything. You follow up the next day to thank her for her time.
